title: Auth & multi-tenancy core
summary: The auth/multi-tenancy core is fundamentally sound and launch-ready with a few hardening items. The load-bearing controls all verify out against live production: the profiles_enforce_immutable trigger blocks role/organization_id self-escalation (only superadmin can move org, only admin/superadmin can change role); get_user_org_id/get_user_role/is_internal_user/is_superadmin are SECURITY DEFINER and REVOKED from anon; all sa_* superadmin RPCs enforce is_superadmin() server-side (the client-side SuperAdminLayout guard is UX only); and — critically — the portal role-gating migration that the source file still labels "NOT APPLIED YET" is in fact fully live: every sensitive tenant table's SELECT/UPDATE requires is_internal_user(), with separate scoped self/opdrachtgever/client-portal policies, so no medewerker or opdrachtgever can read tenant-wide data. A targeted RLS sweep of 22 sensitive tables found zero org-wide leaks. The main launch risks are not authz holes but error-UX (ErrorBoundary renders raw error.message to users), a fail-open feature-flag default, disabled leaked-password protection, and an unauthenticated org-registration endpoint with no rate limiting. None of these leak cross-tenant data; they are first-sprint hardening.
strengths: Profile role/organization_id immutability is enforced by DB trigger, blocking privilege escalation and tenant-hopping
Portal role-gating (is_internal_user) is fully applied in production despite the migration file saying 'NOT APPLIED YET'
Superadmin actions are server-enforced; client-side guard is correctly non-load-bearing
Auth helper functions are SECURITY DEFINER and revoked from anon; login error is plain Dutch

title: Candidates (kandidaten)
summary: The internal candidate UI is solid: tenant isolation via RLS on `candidates`/`documents` is correctly gated with `is_internal_user()`, BSN/IBAN stay Vault-encrypted behind an org-scoped decrypt RPC that returns plain Dutch "Geen toegang", and the prior audit's HIGH H5 (candidate_profile_tokens RLS missing internal-gate) is now FIXED in production — all three token policies carry `is_internal_user()`. However, the PUBLIC surface is not launch-ready. Two confirmed blockers: (1) the public profile page silently drops uploaded CVs/photos because it tries an anon storage upload into an `{authenticated}`-only bucket, swallows the RLS error, and still shows "Bedankt!" — a real data-loss flow once external candidates use it; (2) the `merge_candidate_records` write RPC is SECURITY DEFINER, granted to every authenticated user, and never checks the caller's own org, so a user from org A who learns two candidate UUIDs from org B can merge/delete org-B records cross-tenant. Add to that: no rate-limit/captcha on `candidate-signup` (unbounded fake-candidate + 15MB-file + urgent-notification spam), and raw Postgres `error.message` surfacing to an anonymous candidate on the public profile page. Verdict: not ready for external tenants until the merge authz gap, the public upload break, and signup abuse controls are addressed.
strengths: candidate_profile_tokens RLS now internal-gated (prior audit H5 fixed)
BSN/IBAN encryption + org-scoped decrypt RPC with Dutch error
Profile tokens use 256-bit CSPRNG entropy

title: Employees & compliance
summary: The module's defensive fundamentals are solid: onboarding tokens use 32-byte CSPRNG entropy, BSN/IBAN written through the public onboarding endpoint are still encrypted by the candidates Vault trigger, the legacy personal_data path uses an explicit column allowlist, contract-sign and onboarding-submit run service-role + token-gated with consistent plain-Dutch error messages, and the compliance check has dynamic rules plus a Dutch-labelled hardcoded fallback with audit-logged overrides. However there are two launch-blocking problems. (1) The checked-in schema still carries anon RLS policies on public.contracts (public_sign_token_select / _update with predicate `sign_token IS NOT NULL`, never dropped in any migration) that let the anon API key read and tamper with EVERY signable contract across ALL tenants directly via PostgREST — a cross-tenant data leak/integrity hole the prior live audit did not list (live-DB state must be verified). (2) The live "Kandidaat in dienst nemen" button routes to EmployeeNew.tsx, a divergent/abandoned flow that writes the legacy employees table and never sets candidates.employee_status or creates candidate_employment, so a hired worker disappears from the Medewerkers list and shows no start date; the correct HireEmployeeSheet.tsx is dead code. Additional medium issues: onboarding-submit mass-assigns any maps_to_column to candidates with no server-side allowlist, the token used_at check is non-atomic (double-submit duplicates docs) with no rate-limiting, contract e-sign evidence trusts a spoofable x-forwarded-for header, and two hire mutations surface raw Supabase error.message to the UI. Verdict: not ready until the anon-contracts policy and the broken hire flow are fixed.
strengths: Onboarding tokens use strong CSPRNG entropy and single-use + expiry semantics
BSN/IBAN submitted through public onboarding are still Vault-encrypted; legacy path uses an explicit column allowlist
Public-facing onboarding and contract pages have consistent plain-Dutch error handling with no raw-error leakage

title: Companies (opdrachtgevers)
summary: The Companies module is functionally solid and tenant isolation on the core read/write paths is genuinely good: SELECT/UPDATE on companies, company_contacts, company_sla and rate_agreements all carry both an org-scope (get_user_org_id()) AND an is_internal_user() gate, DELETE additionally requires the admin role, and all create/edit flows write organization_id explicitly and log to the audit trail. However, two real launch-impacting gaps exist. (1) The client_portal_invites table has a single FOR ALL policy scoped only on organization_id with NO is_internal_user() gate — a low-privileged medewerker or opdrachtgever portal user (15 such accounts live) can read, forge and renew the UUID activation tokens that grant client-portal access, then seize an opdrachtgever account via the public client-portal-activate function. The deferral was explicitly acknowledged in a migration comment and never closed. (2) The INSERT (tenant_insert) policies on companies and company_contacts are role {public} and org-scoped only, missing the is_internal_user() gate that SELECT/UPDATE have, letting portal-only users inject rows. Secondary issues: kvk-lookup is gateway-unauthenticated (verify_jwt=false) with no rate-limiting and burns a shared paid KVK API key for any logged-in user; raw error.message/KVK error text is surfaced to the UI in several flows instead of plain Dutch; and the company/contact list search interpolates raw input into a PostgREST .or() filter (contained by RLS, but can error/broaden within-org). Verdict: not launch-ready for external tenants until the client_portal_invites RLS gate is added; the rest are first-sprint hardening.
strengths: Strong tenant isolation + admin-gated delete + audit logging on companies/contacts core paths
KVK lookup edge function does in-body auth and returns plain-Dutch not-found, no SSRF (fixed upstream URLs)

title: Placements (plaatsingen)
summary: The Placements module is functionally rich and tenant isolation is fundamentally sound: all read/update paths go through RLS with both org-scope and is_internal_user() gates, and the placement-confirmation edge function authenticates the caller, derives org server-side from the profile, fetches the placement via the user-scoped (RLS-protected) client, and returns a generic 500 instead of leaking internals. Net: data-integrity and error-UX issues block external go-live; no confirmed cross-tenant leak.

Both edge functions do Bearer self-auth; send-timesheet-approval is org-scoped, status-filtered, HTML-escaped, audit/communications-logged, and covered by the outbound kill-switch. However, the core data-entry paths are broken by the candidates/employees merge: both manual entry and CSV import resolve a legacy employees row that the current hire flow never creates, while timesheets.employee_id is still NOT NULL — so timesheet entry fails for every worker hired through the live app. validate-timesheets also reverts already-approved timesheets back to AI colors with no status guard, and raw Postgres errors leak to the Dutch UI. This is not a data-leak risk but it is a correctness/data-integrity blocker. Verdict: not launch-ready for external tenants until the employees-table dependency and the approval-revert are fixed.
strengths: RLS defense-in-depth: internal tenant gate + employee/client self-policies + column-whitelisting triggers
SECURITY DEFINER triggers enforce per-role timesheet state machine + hours bounds server-side
Email approval function: org-scoped, status-filtered, kill-switch-covered, HTML-escaped, audit-logged

title: Invoicing & Exact Online
summary: The invoicing/Exact module rests on solid foundations: invoice RLS (SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE) carries the is_internal_user() gate, next_invoice_number enforces tenant authz with an atomic sequence + UNIQUE(org, invoice_number), the exact-api proxy is genuinely SSRF-hardened (the voys-api style open-proxy bug from the prior audit was NOT repeated here — it blocks absolute URLs, control chars, traversal and unknown methods, and role-gates to admin/backoffice/finance), and the Exact token is fetched fresh per call and never exposed to the client. The webhook applies a forward-only status guard and sync is idempotent (exact_invoice_id 409 guard). However there are real launch risks: raw Exact/Postgres error strings leak to the recruiter UI in several client + edge paths (violating the plain-Dutch mandate); exact-sync-invoice and exact-sync-account lack the role gate that exact-api has, so a low-priv internal user can drive Exact writes; generate-invoice-pdf persists a getPublicUrl on the private documents bucket (latent world-readable invoices with KVK/BTW/line items); the public exact-webhook decrypts EVERY org's secret on each unauthenticated request (DoS amplification) with a non-constant-time compare and no HMAC; and the invoice INSERT RLS policy still lacks the internal-user gate. None require a redesign. Verdict: ready-with-conditions — fix the error-leak and getPublicUrl items before external tenants; the rest is first hardening sprint.
strengths: exact-api proxy is SSRF-hardened — the voys-api open-proxy pattern was NOT repeated
Strong role + tenant gating on exact-api and exact-register

title: Housing (huisvesting)
summary: The Housing module is functionally mature and its core tenant-isolation is sound: every housing table has RLS scoped to organization_id, SELECT on properties/units/assignments/inspections/keys is gated behind is_internal_user(), the v_unit_occupancy view is security_invoker=true (so it leaks nothing cross-tenant), and BSN/IBAN never appear here. The overbooking guard (check_unit_capacity trigger) does block the ordinary sequential double-booking with a clean Dutch message, and the UI has thoughtful client-side pre-checks for capacity, deletion-with-history, and moves. However there are real launch-blocking-class gaps: (1) the INSERT RLS policies on housing_assignments/units/properties/inspections/key_registrations are on role {public} with NO is_internal_user() gate, so a low-privileged medewerker/opdrachtgever portal user can write (pollute/abuse) housing data in their own org via PostgREST even though they cannot read it; (2) the overbooking trigger uses a non-locking COUNT and is therefore not race-safe — concurrent inserts/moves can exceed capacity; (3) there is no DB-level uniqueness preventing one candidate occupying two units and no check_in<check_out constraint, so integrity relies entirely on client-side filtering; and (4) nearly every housing mutation surfaces raw e.message to a toast, leaking Postgres/PostgREST English on any non-trigger failure (FK RESTRICT, NOT NULL, network/RLS). None require redesign — they are targeted RLS, constraint, and error-wrapping fixes. Verdict: ready with conditions before external multi-tenant exposure.
strengths: Tenant isolation on all housing tables is correct and view does not leak cross-tenant
Overbooking guard trigger + status-sync trigger enforce capacity with a plain-Dutch error
Layered client-side guards on assign / move / delete flows

risks.title: Overbooking trigger is not race-safe — concurrent inserts/moves can exceed capacity
risks.evidence: check_unit_capacity() runs a plain non-locking SELECT count(*) FROM housing_assignments WHERE unit_id=new.unit_id ... then compares to capacity, with no row lock on units and no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (contrast sync_unit_status_from_assignments which does FOR UPDATE). Under READ COMMITTED two concurrent assign/move transactions both read occupancy=N<capacity, both pass, both commit.
risks.impact: Two intercedenten (or a double-click / two browser tabs) assigning the last bed of a unit simultaneously both succeed, producing an over-capacity unit that violates SNF/permit limits (max_persons_permit). The CLAUDE.md claim 'DB trigger blocks overbooking' holds only for the sequential case.
risks.rec: Inside check_unit_capacity(), take a lock before counting — e.g. PERFORM 1 FROM units WHERE id = new.unit_id FOR UPDATE; (or a unit-scoped advisory lock) so concurrent transactions serialize on the unit. Optionally back it with an exclusion/partial-unique guarantee.

risks.evidence: pg_constraint on housing_assignments shows only PK, FKs and the payment_frequency CHECK — no unique index on (candidate_id) for active rows, no CHECK (check_out_date IS NULL OR check_out_date >= check_in_date). De-duplication of residents relies entirely on ResidentsTab.tsx availableEmployees client filter (occupiedIds, 78-100); check_in/out ordering is purely UI.
risks.impact: A race between two assign flows, a move that crosses with an assign, or a crafted PostgREST insert can place the same person in two active units at once (double housing-deduction, wrong occupancy counts). check_out_date can be set before check_in_date, corrupting tenure history and overdue-rent logi
risks.rec: Add a partial unique index on housing_assignments(candidate_id) WHERE status IN ('ingecheckt','gereserveerd'), and a CHECK (check_out_date IS NULL OR check_out_date >= check_in_date). Surface a Dutch message on the resulting unique-violation.

title: Transport & vehicles
summary: The Transport module is one of the better-built areas: tenant isolation runs through `get_user_org_id()` RLS, SELECT/UPDATE on the core vehicle tables were hardened with `is_internal_user()` in migration 20260422130000, the damage-report email is correctly fenced with role gating (external forward = admin/backoffice only), a route_status state machine, server-side HTML escaping, short-TTL signed photo URLs, and the outbound kill-switch. No critical data-leak or cross-tenant break was confirmable in the code I read. The launch-blocking concerns are softer: every mutation surfaces raw Supabase/Postgres `error.message` to Dutch recruiters (error-UX mandate violation), `rdw-lookup` interpolates the license plate into the RDW SODA URL without encoding (SoQL/param injection) and has no role/internal gate, and the client-side multi-step "hard delete" of a vehicle is non-atomic so a mid-sequence failure orphans rows/photos. RLS on INSERT/DELETE for vehicles/fuel/damage/mileage could not be verified from the local migrations (they predate the captured history and only SELECT/UPDATE were re-gated), so the internal-only write gate is unconfirmed and must be checked against the live DB before external tenants. Overall: ship-able after a focused hardening pass, not before.
strengths: Core vehicle tables SELECT/UPDATE are gated with is_internal_user() (portal/opdrachtgever excluded)
send-damage-report enforces role + state-machine + kill-switch + Dutch errors
Damage/fine photos served via short-TTL signed URLs, bucket stays private
check-vehicle-apk is idempotent and cron-secret gated; user-mode is org-scoped

risks.rec: Validate the plate against ^[A-Z0-9]{4,8}$ and reject otherwise; use encodeURIComponent on the value; add an is_internal_user()/role check (a medewerker has no reason to call RDW). Reconcile config.toml (verify_jwt=false) with the doc.

risks.title: Vehicle hard-delete is a non-atomic multi-statement client-side sequence — partial failure orphans data and storage
risks.evidence: src/pages/VehicleDetail.tsx:102-135 — sequential awaits: storage.remove(damagePhotos) → storage.remove(finePhotos) → delete fuel_card_transactions → delete vehicle_damage_reports → delete vehicle_assignments → delete vehicles, with no transaction; photos are removed BEFORE the row deletes (:117-122)
risks.impact: If any middle step fails (RLS denial on one child table, network drop, FK still blocking), the operation aborts mid-way: photos are already deleted from storage while the damage/fine rows still reference them, or some child rows are gone while the vehicle remains — leaving inconsistent state and bro
risks.rec: Move the cascade into a SECURITY DEFINER RPC (single DB transaction) that deletes children then the vehicle, and only purge storage objects after the transaction commits. At minimum, delete DB rows before storage objects so a failure never strands live rows pointing at deleted photos.

risks.title: INSERT/DELETE RLS on vehicles, fuel_card_transactions, vehicle_damage_reports, mileage_entries is not verifiable in repo and may lack the is_internal_user() gate
risks.evidence: migration 20260422130000 only re-creates tenant_select/tenant_update for these tables (lines 179-417); no CREATE POLICY ... FOR INSERT/DELETE for vehicles/fuel_card_transactions/vehicle_damage_reports/mileage_entries exists anywhere under supabase/migrations/ (grep returns none); the tables' original policies predate the captured history (Lovable era). Portal write path PortalVehicle.tsx:89 inserts directly into vehicle_damage_reports via PostgREST, so a medewerker INSERT policy must exist live.
risks.impact: If the surviving INSERT policies are the common org-scope-only `{public}` form (matching the prior audit's MEDIUM 'PII tenant_insert missing is_internal_user()'), a low-privileged portal/opdrachtgever user could insert fuel transactions, mileage rows, or damage reports for their org — data pollution
risks.rec: Query the live DB (get pg_policies for these 4 tables) and confirm INSERT/DELETE carry org-scope AND either is_internal_user() (internal tables) or a tightly scoped self-policy (the portal damage-insert). Add explicit, repo-tracked policies so main==production and the gate is auditable.

risks.title: Fuel-card import and fiscal-mileage analysis run heavy multi-query joins fully client-side with no server validation
risks.evidence: src/pages/FuelCardAnalysis.tsx:1036-1418 — handleImport fetches vehicles+assignments+placements (incl. candidate address_lat/lng), computes fraud flags and writes fuel_card_transactions + vehicle current_mileage entirely in the browser; FiscalMileageAnalysis.tsx:133-225 generateReviews builds fiscal_mileage_reviews client-side
risks.impact: Flagging logic (over-capacity, multiple/day, route-consumption fraud) and km/fuel-card overwrites are trivially bypassable or manipulable by a user editing the payload, and the import does no server-side size/row cap (a large CSV/XLSX loops unbounded in 100-row insert batches). Integrity of the frau
risks.rec: Longer-term, move the import + flagging into an edge function (server-side validation, row cap, single transaction). Short-term acceptable given internal-only actors, but document it as known debt.

risks.title: Vehicle plate/notes free-text and damage description rendered without explicit sanitization in some internal UI cells
risks.evidence: src/pages/Transport.tsx:221 title={v.notes} and {v.notes}; VehicleDamageTab.tsx:205 {r.description} — React auto-escapes so no XSS, but FuelCardAnalysis raw_data (uploaded CSV cell values) is stored in jsonb and re-rendered (FuelCardAnalysis.tsx:1455 {r[h]} preview)
risks.impact: No stored-XSS sink found (React escapes JSX text and the email path uses escapeHtml), so this is informational/defense-in-depth: untrusted CSV/plate/notes content is persisted verbatim. Risk would only materialize if any of these fields are later piped into an HTML email or dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
risks.rec: Keep relying on React escaping; ensure any future export/email of vehicle notes, plate, or fuel raw_data goes through the existing escapeHtml/DOMPurify path. No action required now.

title: Communication & kill-switch
summary: The kill-switch (outbound-pause) is genuinely well-engineered: it gates every heavy outbound path (interactive Outlook send, all template mailers via sendViaOutlookAccount, whatsapp-send, bulk-campaign-processor, email-campaign-processor, automated-messages onboarding reminders), fails safe, and logs blocked messages as recoverable 'concept' rows rather than dropping them. Email sending is correctly gated to internal roles, HTML-sanitized, and attachment-size-capped. Opt-out is enforced server-side inside the get_campaign_candidates RPC for both channels. However, the WhatsApp/bulk family of edge functions authenticates only with getAuthenticatedOrg (valid JWT + org), with NO internal-role gate — confirmed that medewerker (employee-portal) users have a profiles row, so a low-privilege portal user could drive whatsapp-send, whatsapp-api, whatsapp-register/disconnect and bulk-campaign-processor against the org's Meta account. Dutch error handling is also undermined at runtime: the useWhatsAppSend hook reads response.error.message, so the carefully-written Dutch opt-out/rate-limit/credential errors are replaced by the raw English 'Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code'. Two functional breakages (dead WhatsApp send on the Communications page; misleading 'success' on a paused send) and an opt-out-only consent model round out the risks. No data-breach-level hole found in this module; gaps are authz-hardening and error-UX. Readiness: ready-with-conditions.
strengths: Kill-switch covers every heavy outbound path and fails safe with recoverable concept-logging
Outlook send path is properly role-gated, HTML-sanitized and attachment-capped
Opt-out is enforced server-side in the campaign candidate RPC for both channels

risks.title: WhatsApp + bulk-campaign edge functions lack an internal-role gate; a medewerker/portal user can drive them
risks.evidence: whatsapp-send/index.ts:26, whatsapp-api/index.ts:25, whatsapp-register/index.ts:19, whatsapp-disconnect/index.ts:16, bulk-campaign-processor/index.ts:56 all call getAuthenticatedOrg (whatsapp-utils.ts:116-147) which only checks JWT validity + profiles.organization_id — no role check. PortalContext.tsx:42-47 confirms medewerker users have a profiles row with role='medewerker' and an organization_id.
risks.impact: A low-privilege employee-portal account (role=medewerker) holds a JWT whose profile has an org_id, so it passes getAuthenticatedOrg. Such a user could call whatsapp-send to message arbitrary numbers as the org, whatsapp-api to read/delete the org's WhatsApp templates/media/QR/profile, whatsapp-regis
risks.rec: Replace getAuthenticatedOrg with requireInternalProfile (or add isInternalRole gating) in whatsapp-send, whatsapp-api, whatsapp-register, whatsapp-disconnect, whatsapp-templates-sync and bulk-campaign-processor, mirroring outlook-send-mail/email-campaign-processor.

risks.title: Dutch error messages from whatsapp-send never reach the user — raw English 'non-2xx' string is shown instead
risks.evidence: src/hooks/useWhatsAppSend.ts:31-33 throws new Error(response.error.message) — supabase-js sets FunctionsHttpError.message to 'Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code' for any non-2xx; the Dutch JSON body (whatsapp-send/index.ts:75 'Kandidaat heeft zich afgemeld voor WhatsApp', :87 'Rate limit bereikt...', :92 'WhatsApp niet geconfigureerd') lives in response.data.error and is discarded. onError shows it via toast (useWhatsAppSend.ts:41-42).
risks.impact: Directly violates the error-UX mandate: a Dutch recruiter who hits opt-out (403), rate limit (429) or unconfigured WhatsApp (400) sees the raw technical English 'Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code' toast instead of the plain-Dutch reason the backend prepared. Confusing and unprofessional o
risks.rec: In useWhatsAppSend, on response.error read the JSON body (await response.error.context?.json() or invoke-with-data fallback) and prefer response.data?.error; surface a Dutch fallback otherwise. Same pattern needed wherever functions.invoke errors are toasted.

risks.title: Paused WhatsApp send is reported to the user as success (no error, no 'concept' notice)
risks.evidence: whatsapp-send/index.ts:181-186 returns 200 with {success:false, paused:true, message:'...concept opgeslagen'}; useWhatsAppSend.ts:31 only branches on response.error (a 200 has none), so onSuccess fires (:37-40) and no toast is shown. The frontend never inspects data.paused/data.success.
risks.impact: When the kill-switch is active, the recruiter clicks send, sees no error and the conversation refreshes — they reasonably believe the message went out, but it was only logged as a concept. Silent non-delivery erodes trust and can cause missed candidate communication once a real tenant forgets the pa
risks.rec: Have useWhatsAppSend inspect response.data?.paused / success and surface a distinct Dutch info toast ('Bericht niet verzonden — WhatsApp staat op pauze, opgeslagen als concept').

risks.title: Manual WhatsApp send from the Communications page is broken (payload shape mismatch)
risks.evidence: src/pages/Communications.tsx:196-203 invokes whatsapp-send with { to, message: formBody, candidate_id, company_id }; whatsapp-send/index.ts:31-35 requires `type` and reads text.body — 'message' is never read, so it returns 400 'Veld to en type zijn verplicht'.
risks.impact: The 'WhatsApp versturen' action on the Communications screen always fails. The catch at Communications.tsx:210-211 then shows 'Versturen mislukt: Edge Function returned a non-2xx status code' — a dead feature plus a raw technical error. Not a security hole but a visibly broken, error-jargon-leaking
risks.rec: Send { to, type:'text', text:{ body: formBody }, candidate_id } and drop the unsupported company_id, or route through useWhatsAppSend.

risks.title: Raw error.message surfaced on manual communication insert
risks.evidence: src/pages/Communications.tsx:164-165 (insert into communications) and :173 onError: (err) => toast.error(err.message) — a DB CHECK/constraint failure (e.g. chk_comm_target requiring candidate_id or company_id) would surface its raw Postgres message to the recruiter.
risks.impact: On a validation failure the user sees a raw Postgres/PostgREST error string rather than plain Dutch. Low likelihood (form normally supplies a target) and low blast radius, but it is an error-jargon leak on a customer screen.
risks.rec: Map known constraint failures to Dutch ('Kies een kandidaat of opdrachtgever') and use a generic Dutch fallback for the rest.

risks.title: WhatsApp webhook status update is not org-scoped (defense-in-depth gap)
risks.evidence: supabase/functions/whatsapp-webhook/index.ts:494-497 — UPDATE communications SET whatsapp_status=... WHERE whatsapp_message_id=messageId, with no .eq('organization_id', orgId). The request is already secret-authenticated to a single org (:46-111), but the write query itself spans tenants.
risks.impact: Practically unexploitable because Meta message IDs (wamid.*) are globally unique, so a cross-tenant collision is not realistic. Still, a per-request authenticated handler writing without an org filter is a latent multi-tenant footgun if message-id assumptions ever change.
risks.rec: Add .eq('organization_id', orgId) to the status-update query for defense-in-depth.

risks.title: Webhook secret comparison is non-constant-time; no Meta HMAC / replay protection
risks.evidence: whatsapp-webhook/index.ts:85,107 (decrypted === / !== webhookSecret) and whatsapp-config/index.ts:43 — plain JS string compare on the shared secret; no X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC verification and no timestamp/replay window. Carried over from prior audit (docs/security-audit-2026-06-10.md:115-116).
risks.impact: Timing side-channel on the shared secret is largely theoretical over the internet; bigger gap is the absence of Meta HMAC + replay protection, so a leaked/guessed secret allows replaying webhook payloads (e.g. re-triggering sick-report cascades or match-status flips). The webhook always returns 200
risks.rec: Verify Meta's X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC, add a timestamp/idempotency window, and use a crypto.subtle constant-time compare. Rate-limit the decrypt-all fallback loop.

risks.title: Rate-limit check and record are non-atomic (TOCTOU)
risks.evidence: check_rate_limit (migration 20260309005718...:200-257) is STABLE/read-only and separate from record_rate_limit; whatsapp-send/index.ts:80-88 then :234-237 and bulk-campaign-processor/index.ts:190-200 then :269-272 do check-then-record with concurrency (processWithConcurrency up to maxConcurrent).
risks.impact: Concurrent sends in the same minute window can all pass the check before any record lands, so the per-org rate cap can be overshot under load. Soft guard only — Meta enforces its own limits — so impact is bounded, but the cap is not a hard ceiling.
risks.rec: Make rate limiting atomic (single SECURITY DEFINER RPC that increments-and-checks in one statement, or a DB-side counter with a unique window row + conditional update).

risks.title: Bulk campaigns are opt-out-only — no consent/legal-basis (opt-in) capture
risks.evidence: src/components/campaigns/CampaignWizard.tsx + SegmentBuilder.tsx contain no consent/toestemming/grondslag gating (grep found none); get_campaign_candidates filters only opted_out. Matches prior audit docs/security-audit-2026-06-10.md:125.
risks.impact: Under AVG, sending bulk WhatsApp/email to candidates relies on an opt-out model with no recorded legal basis or opt-in. For a labor-migrant audience this is a compliance exposure once external tenants run campaigns at scale, though not a data breach.
risks.rec: Record a per-candidate legal basis / opt-in for marketing-style bulk sends and surface it in the wizard; first hardening sprint.

title: AI dossier / CV analysis
summary: The primary analyze-cv pipeline (VPS/Gemini/Cloud) is well-engineered for a launch: strict tenant checks on every candidate read/write, server-side AVG-pseudonymization of dossier text, layered anti-prompt-injection (hardcoded system prompt + org-addendum sanitization + dossier delimiter-wrapping + forced schema output), a race-safe SECURITY DEFINER credit ledger with FOR UPDATE, append-only usage + audit logging, and consistently plain-Dutch user errors in the main flow. However it is NOT launch-ready as-is because of the legacy cv-rewrite function, which ships raw candidate PII (name, email, phone, date_of_birth, nationality, city) to a third-party Lovable AI gateway with no pseudonymization and only partial anonymization — a clear AVG breach the prior audit missed. Two prior-audit AVG findings (Gemini-vision raw scans to Google; NL-only PII regexes leaving foreign migrant PII unredacted) are still present in the current tree. Secondary issues: analyze-cv has no role gate so any org member (incl. medewerker/finance) can drain Cloud/Gemini credits and read any in-org dossier; several raw technical error strings (VPS body, fetch/Postgres messages) surface to the recruiter UI; analyze-cv-callback authenticates the VPS worker with a non-constant-time === comparison and has no idempotency/replay guard. Fix cv-rewrite and the vision/PII AVG gaps before exposing real external tenants; the core credit and injection defenses are solid.
strengths: Strong tenant isolation on every candidate read and write in the analyze-cv pipeline
Race-safe credit ledger via SECURITY DEFINER consume_ai_credits with SELECT FOR UPDATE and no overdraft
Layered anti-prompt-injection and org-prompt sanitization across all providers
Privacy-aware vision gating, stale-run recovery, and silent-fail audit/usage logging keep the main flow robust

risks.title: cv-rewrite leaks raw candidate PII (incl. DOB + nationality) to third-party Lovable AI gateway with no pseudonymization
risks.evidence: supabase/functions/cv-rewrite/index.ts:31-36 selects first_name,last_name,email,phone,date_of_birth,nationality,address_city; :85-91 JSON.stringifies the full candidate object into the user prompt; :93-96 POSTs to https://ai.gateway.lovable.dev with model google/gemini-3-flash-preview. Anonymous mode (:67-78) only overwrites name/email/phone/address — date_of_birth and nationality are NOT stripped and flow through even when anonymous=true. No call to pseudonymizeCv anywhere in the file.
risks.impact: AVG/GDPR breach: direct identifying personal data (name, email, phone, DOB, nationality) of labor migrants is transmitted to a US-routed Lovable third-party LLM proxy with no processor agreement, no EU residency, and no pseudonymization — worse than the vision-path issue the prior audit flagged. The
risks.rec: Before external launch: either (a) route cv-rewrite through the same pseudonymizeCv + EU Gemini/VPS path as analyze-cv, or (b) drop the Lovable gateway and use the org-configured provider with a processor agreement. At minimum, in anonymous mode also strip date_of_birth and nationality. Confirm whet

risks.title: Gemini-vision path sends raw, non-pseudonymizable CV scans (name + photo + address) to Google — prior-audit AVG finding still present
risks.evidence: analyze-cv/index.ts:55-76 loadVisionFileParts downloads raw document bytes; :345-358 sends them as inlineData to Gemini; gemini-cv.ts:165-174 attaches inlineData base64 to the Google generativelanguage US endpoint. candidate-dossier.ts:332-360 resolveCvVisionFile restricts to CV-type/CV-named files, but the raw image/PDF (containing the real name, photo, address) cannot be pseudonymized — only the parallel text is.
risks.impact: Identifying PII of arbeidsmigranten reaches Google's US endpoint unredacted whenever a CV is an image/scanned PDF. The code comments acknowledge this explicitly. Repeats finding from docs/security-audit-2026-06-10.md:93 — still unmitigated in the current working tree.
risks.rec: Gate vision behind an explicit per-org opt-in with a documented EU/processor grondslag + DPIA, or restrict vision to OCR'd-then-pseudonymized text only. Do not enable Gemini-vision by default for external tenants.

risks.title: Pseudonymization only covers NL phone/IBAN — foreign migrant PII leaks to the LLM (prior-audit finding still present)
risks.evidence: cv-pseudonymize.ts:72-81 phone regex only matches +31/0031/0 NL prefixes; :93 IBAN regex is /NL\d{2}[A-Z]{4}\d{10}/ (NL-only). No address, no foreign national ID, no passport number, no non-NL phone/IBAN handling. The candidate base is explicitly labor migrants (PL/RO/etc.).
risks.impact: Polish/Romanian/etc. phone numbers, foreign IBANs, and national IDs in CV text pass through to the VPS/Gemini/Cloud LLM unredacted, undermining the AVG-minimization claim for exactly the population this product serves. Repeats docs/security-audit-2026-06-10.md:94.
risks.rec: Broaden phone/IBAN regexes to international formats (general IBAN pattern, E.164-style numbers) and consider stripping address lines, or add a lightweight NER pass. Track residual leakage in cv_pseudonymization_meta.

risks.title: analyze-cv (single) has no role gate — any org member can drain Cloud/Gemini credits and analyze any in-org candidate
risks.evidence: analyze-cv/index.ts:139-166 authenticates only that the user has a profile with organization_id; there is no role check (grep for role/intercedent/finance/medewerker returns nothing functional). Contrast analyze-cv-batch/index.ts:331-337 which requires role==='admin' or superadmin. The credit-spend path (:296-475) is reachable by any authenticated org user; the only candidate guard is organization_id equality (:191-193).
risks.impact: A low-privilege role (finance, backoffice, or a medewerker/portal user whose profile carries an organization_id) can repeatedly trigger paid Cloud/Gemini analyses, draining the org's credit balance (cost-abuse / financial DoS), and force-read/refresh AI dossiers on any candidate in the org. Not a cr
risks.rec: Restrict analyze-cv to internal roles (reuse requireInternalProfile / isInternalRole from _shared/auth.ts) and consider a per-user/per-org rate limit on paid provider calls. At minimum block the medewerker role.

risks.title: Raw technical error strings (VPS body, fetch/Postgres messages) surfaced to the recruiter UI
risks.evidence: analyze-cv/index.ts:533 returns details: errBody (raw VPS worker body); :541 'Kan VPS niet bereiken: ${fetchErr.message}'; :563 outer catch returns 'Fout: ${error.message}' (raw). gemini-cv.ts:187 throws 'Gemini API ${status}: ${text.slice(0,500)}' and anthropic-cv.ts:114 similarly — these bubble up via analyze-cv:373 'Gemini/Cloud-analyse mislukt: ${msg}'. CandidateAiTab.tsx:69-73 extractFunctionErrorMessage renders error+details verbatim in a toast.
risks.impact: A Dutch recruiter can see raw provider/Postgres/HTTP fragments (e.g. truncated Gemini JSON errors, Supabase column errors, VPS stack text) instead of plain Dutch, violating the error-UX mandate and potentially leaking internal infra details (URLs, model ids, provider status text).
risks.rec: Map provider/DB failures to generic plain-Dutch messages for the UI (e.g. 'AI-analyse tijdelijk niet beschikbaar, probeer later opnieuw') and keep raw detail only in console.error / server logs. Do not return details/errBody/error.message to the client.

risks.title: analyze-cv-callback: non-constant-time worker-secret compare and no idempotency/replay guard
risks.evidence: analyze-cv-callback/index.ts:36 'authHeader !== `Bearer ${OLLAMA_API_KEY}`' is a plain string compare (timing side-channel; also noted generally at docs/security-audit-2026-06-10.md:116). The handler (:93-151) unconditionally writes the analysis and inserts audit/usage rows on every call — no check that candidate.ai_status is still 'analyzing' or that this candidate hasn't already been completed, so a replayed callback overwrites results and double-logs usage.
risks.impact: Anyone able to guess/observe OLLAMA_API_KEY timing could brute-force it; more practically, a duplicated or replayed VPS callback (or a stale one after a stale-reset in analyze-cv-batch:422-425) silently overwrites a candidate's analysis and inflates ai_usage_log. Low likelihood, data-integrity impac
risks.rec: Use a constant-time compare (crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual-style) for the worker secret, and make the write conditional on the candidate still being in 'analyzing' state (or include/verify a per-job token) to make the callback idempotent.

risks.title: Batch sync path: preflight credit check is per-candidate, allowing a small overspend window at balance edge
risks.evidence: analyze-cv-batch/index.ts:34-36 comment + :214-219 preflight reads balance before the provider call but consume_ai_credits (:248-260) is the only race-safe gate; with SYNC_CONCURRENCY=4 (:36) up to 3 paid provider calls can complete and then fail the atomic decrement, producing real provider cost with no credit deducted.
risks.impact: At most a few cents of un-billed Gemini/Anthropic usage per exhausted run — the ledger never goes negative (consume_ai_credits is FOR UPDATE), so it is a minor revenue-leak, not a data/integrity problem. Explicitly acknowledged in code.
risks.rec: Acceptable for launch as documented. If tightened later, pre-reserve credits before the provider call or set SYNC_CONCURRENCY=1 near the balance floor.

title: Talentpools (dynamic)
summary: The dynamic Talentpools module is one of the better-isolated parts of the codebase: tenant scoping is enforced by RLS on both `talentpools` and `talentpool_members` (org via `get_user_org_id()`), the cron mode is gated behind a constant-time-ish `CRON_SECRET` header and scopes every pool's candidate query to that pool's own `organization_id`, and the single-pool mode correctly fetches the pool through an RLS-aware user client before letting the service-role admin client mutate it. I found NO cross-tenant data-leak or anonymous-abuse path I can confirm in code. The real launch risks are correctness/UX, not breach: a status-filter dropdown offering enum values (`beschikbaar`, `inactief`) that do not exist on candidates while omitting common ones (`werkzoekend`), so filters silently return zero or wrong members; raw `error.message` from Postgres/PostgREST surfaced into Dutch-recruiter toasts on every mutation; and an unbounded `filter_criteria` jsonb with a 5000-row service-role scan that a tenant admin can use to bulk-insert members. Readiness: ready-with-conditions — fix the status-enum mismatch and the raw-error toasts before external tenants, harden the rest in the first sprint.
strengths: Tenant isolation enforced by RLS on both talentpools and talentpool_members
Cron mode requires CRON_SECRET and per-pool org scoping prevents cross-tenant bleed
Single-pool refresh authorizes via RLS-aware user client before service-role mutation
added_by_filter flag preserves manually-added members across refresh (idempotent diff)

LeadFunnelBoard.tsx:163,190 shows 'werkzoekend' is the primary active-candidate status in production use.

The pool looks broken or, worse, silently empties on every cron refresh (toRemove drops all filter mem
risks.rec: Replace the hardcoded STATUSES list in PoolFilterBuilder with the real candidate_status enum (drive it from a shared constant or the statusLabel map already in TalentpoolDetail.tsx:58-61). Add 'werkzoekend','in_screening','niet_beschikbaar','uitgeschreven','lead'; remove 'beschikbaar','inactief'. Sa

risks.title: Raw Postgres/PostgREST error.message surfaced directly into Dutch recruiter toasts on every mutation
risks.evidence: Talentpools.tsx:110,162 onError: (e:any)=>toast.error(e.message); TalentpoolDetail.tsx:132,149,165,181,196,221 all do toast.error(e.message); FilterPreviewSheet.tsx:113 and AddCandidateSheet.tsx:77 same. Edge function also returns raw matchErr.message ('Filter-query mislukt: ...'), insErr.message, delErr.message (refresh-talentpool-members index.ts:82,92,115,129) which TalentpoolDetail.tsx:213-214 then toasts verbatim.
risks.impact: When a constraint, RLS denial, FK violation, or PostgREST error occurs, the recruiter sees raw technical English/Postgres strings (e.g. 'new row violates row-level security policy', 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint talentpool_members_pkey', 'invalid input value for enum candidate_stat
risks.rec: Map known error codes to plain Dutch in the onError handlers (e.g. PK violation -> 'Kandidaat zit al in deze pool', RLS/permission -> 'Geen toegang', generic -> 'Er ging iets mis bij het opslaan'). Never pass e.message / matchErr.message straight to toast.error. Apply across all six mutations + the

title: Employee & Client portals
summary: The portal data-isolation core is genuinely strong: live RLS confirms tenant-wide tables are gated with is_internal_user(), client-portal access is narrowed via get_client_portal_company_id(), and timesheet write paths are defended by three SECURITY DEFINER triggers that raise plain-Dutch exceptions and block a medewerker/opdrachtgever from touching anything but their allowed fields. Invite tokens have strong entropy (uuid / 32-byte hex) and 7-day expiry, and PortalDocuments uses short-lived signed URLs. The prior audit's H5 (candidate_profile_tokens) is now FIXED in production. However three prior issues remain and four new code-confirmed holes exist: H1 (send-portal-invite still returns an account-takeover activation token with zero authz) and H3 (ziekmelding nature-of-illness still auto-emailed to the inlener — AVG art.9) are unremediated, and live RLS shows leftover org-wide {public} policies on vehicle_damage_reports that let any portal user read/modify every colleague's damage reports, plus an unguarded candidate_self_update (no WITH CHECK, no immutability trigger) letting a medewerker overwrite their own employee_status/ai_*/PII fields. Portal login pages also surface raw English Supabase auth errors instead of the Dutch string the main app uses. Verdict: not launch-ready for external tenants until H1, H3 and the vehicle_damage_reports policy leak are closed; the rest are first-sprint hardening.
strengths: Defense-in-depth: client-portal timesheet write paths are locked down by SECURITY DEFINER triggers
Defense-in-depth: client-portal scoping function + self-policies correctly isolate opdrachtgever and medewerker data

title: Superadmin & integrations (Carerix/Voys/MS/sourcing)
summary: The superadmin control plane is the strongest part of this module: every sa_* RPC and topup_ai_credits enforces is_superadmin() server-side, the sensitive integration-credential RPCs (get_voys_token, get_carerix_token) are service-role-grant-only, and RLS on org_modules/credits/usage/domains/carerix/voys/job-data is correctly tenant- and role-scoped, so the client-side superadmin gate being cosmetic does not create exposure. The Carerix sync pipeline, Outlook OAuth callback (HMAC-signed single-use DB-backed state), data-export and domain-management are all well-authorized (admin/internal gates, org-scoping, audit logging, Dutch errors). The blocking problem is voys-api: the prior audit's H2 (anonymous SSRF open-proxy + per-org Voys-token exfiltration) is STILL fully present in the current tree — both the unauthenticated api_token bypass and the endpoint.startsWith('http') arbitrary-URL fetch. Secondary issues: four paid-external-API / org-mutating edge functions (apify-job-import, linkedin-job-search, exa-people-search, voys-sync-calls) authenticate any org profile but lack an internal-role gate, so the 15 existing medewerker/opdrachtgever portal users can burn paid Apify/Exa credits or trigger org-wide call syncs; carerix-config has admin-gated SSRF via instance_url; and several integration error paths surface raw upstream/Postgres strings rather than Dutch. Verdict: not launch-ready until voys-api is fixed; the rest is first-sprint hardening.
strengths: Superadmin RPC layer fully enforces is_superadmin() server-side
Integration credential RPCs are service-role-grant-only and Vault-encrypted

title: Rate limiting / DDoS / IP-blocking / WAF / bot protection
summary: The platform has ZERO request-level abuse protection at every layer that an external attacker can reach. vercel.json contains only an SPA rewrite — no Vercel Firewall/WAF, no BotID, no security headers, no rate-limit rules (confirmed). No captcha/Turnstile/hCaptcha exists anywhere in src/ or supabase/. The only rate limiting in the codebase is per-org outbound-channel quota (check_rate_limit/record_rate_limit against rate_limit_tracking) used exclusively by the bulk-campaign/whatsapp-send senders; there is NO per-request or per-IP limiting on any of the ~14 verify_jwt=false public/anon edge functions, which are directly reachable at ${SUPABASE_URL}/functions/v1/... using the public anon apikey shipped in the frontend bundle. The highest-impact exposures: register-organization (anonymous, no captcha, auto-confirms email, and every org INSERT fires the organizations_create_credits trigger seeding €50 of real spend on the SHARED ANTHROPIC_API_KEY — scriptable unbounded financial loss, audit H6 still 100% present); candidate-signup (anonymous, writes candidate PII + uploads up to 15MB to storage + creates tasks/notifications per call — DB/storage flooding + leaks raw err.message to the client); and both webhooks (whatsapp-webhook/exact-webhook) which, on any unmatched secret, loop over every active org config and call a Vault decrypt RPC per config — an anonymous Vault-decrypt-amplification DoS. A separate NEW high-confidence finding: a live anon UPDATE RLS policy on contracts (public_sign_token_update ... USING(sign_token IS NOT NULL)) appears to allow unauthenticated mass-corruption of all signable contracts. Verdict for this dimension: NOT READY — the platform would be trivially abused (financially and via DoS) the moment it is exposed to real external tenants on the public internet.
strengths: Per-org outbound campaign rate limiting exists and is correctly applied (genuine strength)
Sensitive edge functions (data-export, match-bulk-notify, send-*) correctly gate on requireInternalProfile (strength)

title: Error UX — plain Dutch vs technical jargon
summary: Pre-submit/inline validation and the dedicated public token pages (Login.tsx, MatchResponse.tsx, ContractSign/Activate pages) are well-localized Dutch — a genuine strength. But the dominant server-error pattern across the app is unsafe: 189 call sites do bare `toast.error(error.message)` / `toast.error(e.message)` (in 109 files) where `error` is a thrown PostgrestError or a DB RAISE EXCEPTION. There is NO central error-translation utility and NO global TanStack `QueryClient`/`MutationCache` onError (App.tsx:108 is a bare `new QueryClient()`), so unexpected DB errors surface verbatim English Postgres strings (RLS denials, FK-RESTRICT on deletes, unique violations) to Dutch recruiters. The database itself raises a mix of Dutch and raw English/developer-format exceptions (e.g. `merge_candidate_records: both candidates have an employees (payroll) record (uuid and uuid); merge these manually`, `Not authorized`, `profiles.id is immutable`) that flow straight into toasts. The two external-facing portal logins leak the raw Supabase `Invalid login credentials` because their Dutch fallback is dead code. This won't leak data or corrupt anything, but it will confuse external tenants and looks unfinished. Readiness: ready-with-conditions — fix the external-facing leaks (portal logins, dedup/merge, FK-delete toasts) before external tenants, then sweep the rest in the first hardening sprint.
strengths: Dedicated public token pages and inline validation are well-localized (strength)

title: Console & network hygiene + performance
summary: Frontend console hygiene is good: only 14 console statements in src/ (all error/warn, no PII), no source maps in the prod build (dist/ verified clean of .map / sourceMappingURL), and all 5 Supabase realtime channels have proper removeChannel cleanup — no subscription churn. The dominant risks are performance/UX, not data leaks. (1) The app ships as a single 3.57 MB monolithic JS bundle: 88 page components are statically imported in App.tsx with zero React.lazy and no manualChunks — a heavy first-load cost for a mobile PWA aimed at labor migrants. (2) QueryClient is constructed with no defaults (staleTime:0, refetchOnWindowFocus:true), which makes the dashboard's ~25 independent useQuery/REST round-trips (Dashboard.tsx Promise.all of 4 + 6 alert queries + 6 DashboardWidgets cards + KpiDashboard + ApkExpiry + NotificationBell poll) re-fire on every window refocus — the root amplifier behind the ~37 calls the orchestrator saw. (3) getPublicUrl() is called on the PRIVATE documents bucket in 7 places, persisting broken/404 links to the DB (cv_file_url, invoices.pdf_url, housing photos) and sending a dead link to Meta in WhatsApp media-send. (4) ~277 toast.error(e.message) sites and ErrorBoundary surface raw Postgres/Supabase strings to Dutch recruiters. None of these block launch, but the bundle size, getPublicUrl breakage, and raw-error UX should be fixed before broad external rollout.
strengths: No source maps in production build
Realtime subscriptions and frontend console use are clean
PWA service worker precaches only static assets — no caching of authenticated/PII responses

title: Security & AVG delta vs 2026-06-10 audit
summary: Verified the 6 HIGH findings from the 2026-06-10 audit against the current working tree: 1 is FIXED (H5 candidate_profile_tokens RLS now has is_internal_user() gate, confirmed live), and 5 remain STILL-OPEN unchanged (H1 send-portal-invite cross-tenant token + token-in-response, H2 voys-api SSRF + api_token auth-bypass, H3 sick-report health data to client, H4 no right-to-erasure, H6 register-organization anonymous abuse). The previously-flagged broad PII tenant_insert MEDIUM gates are now substantially fixed (remaining insert policies are properly self-scoped). The matching-stage2 WIP (rerank-matches/gemini-rerank) is competently built (RLS-scoped auth, credit guard, anti-injection, generic error returns) but introduces a NEW AVG gap: it sends the candidate's real full name + AI summary to Google Gemini (US endpoint) with no pseudonymization, contradicting the platform's documented AVG-pseudonymization standard. Two public anonymous endpoints (candidate-signup, candidate-profile) leak raw Postgres/Supabase error.message strings and lack any rate-limiting/captcha. The other new functions audited (translate-platform, domain-management, whatsapp-disconnect, birthday-loyalty-cron, match-bulk-notify) are well-secured. Not launch-ready for external tenants until H1/H2 (real exploitable bugs) and the AVG cluster (H3/H4 + rerank pseudonymization) are closed.
strengths: H5 FIXED: candidate_profile_tokens RLS now enforces is_internal_user()
MEDIUM mostly FIXED: broad PII tenant_insert policies replaced with self-scoped insert policies
Strength: shared edge auth helper is robust and used by the new functions

title: UI/UX consistency & accessibility
summary: The app has a solid shadcn/Radix foundation, a single consistent toast system (sonner), a working ErrorBoundary with plain-Dutch copy, good public-page error handling, and a reusable EntityLink primitive — so the happy path looks polished. But under the surface there are two launch-blocking-class quality problems for external Dutch tenants. First, error UX leaks: ~189 mutation handlers do toast.error(e.message) with no Dutch fallback, and because mutations throw the raw Supabase/Postgres error, recruiters will see English technical strings ("new row violates row-level security policy", "duplicate key value...") instead of plain Dutch. Second, accessibility is weak: 99 of 108 icon-only buttons have no accessible name, 27 Dialog/AlertDialog instances ship without a Description (the aria-describedby warning the orchestrator saw, multiplied), and form validation is effectively ad-hoc (only 1 file uses react-hook-form/Zod and FormMessage despite CLAUDE.md claiming otherwise). Consistency gaps compound this: 9 destructive flows (incl. bulk campaign send) use unstyled native window.confirm, several deletes fire with no confirmation at all, loading states are split three ways (Skeleton / spinner / "Laden..." text), dark mode is configured but entirely dead (no .dark CSS, 41 orphan dark: variants, next-themes unused), and the multi-tenant accent color has no contrast clamp so a pale brand color makes 205 text-primary usages unreadable. None of these breach data, but several will visibly confuse a recruiter or look unprofessional to a new tenant.
strengths: Strengths: consistent single toast system, working ErrorBoundary+global logging, reusable EntityLink primitive, good public-page error copy

title: Auth & multi-tenant isolation (deep)
summary: The tenant-isolation foundation is genuinely strong and has materially improved since the 2026-06-10 audit. All core RLS helpers (get_user_org_id, get_user_role, is_superadmin, is_internal_user) are STABLE SECURITY DEFINER, keyed on auth.uid() reading profiles/superadmins with a locked search_path — unspoofable from the client. The profiles self-escalation guard (enforce_profile_immutable_fields trigger) correctly blocks role/organization_id/id changes by non-admins/non-superadmins, all six sa_* superadmin RPCs carry real is_superadmin() body guards, and the four auth zones are cleanly separated (useOrganizationId is used only in AppLayout/AuthProvider routes, never in portal or superadmin). I verified against the LIVE production database (read-only) that the prior-audit items have largely been remediated: tenant_insert on candidates/documents/placements/contracts/timesheets/sick_reports/communications now carries is_internal_user() (the audit MEDIUM — FIXED), candidate_profile_tokens RLS is internal-only (prior HIGH — FIXED), match_proposal_tokens has no anon-reachable SELECT (SEC-4 — live), and voys/exact/whatsapp/carerix token RPCs are REVOKED from anon. The remaining risks are not catastrophic but should be closed before external tenants: an unfixed cross-tenant token-disclosure path in send-portal-invite, four security migrations applied to production but NOT mirrored locally (config drift that breaks CI/local reproducibility and review), a candidate self-update policy with no WITH CHECK on organization_id, broad default GRANT ALL to anon on every PII table with RLS not FORCEd (zero defense-in-depth — safe today only because every policy gates on auth.uid()), and pervasive raw error.message surfacing that will leak Postgres RLS-denial jargon to Dutch recruiters. Verdict: ready with conditions for the single-tenant JA Werkt launch; close the cross-tenant invite path and mirror the drifted migrations before onboarding additional external tenants.
strengths: Core auth helpers, profile immutability, sa_* guards and zone separation are correctly implemented
Prior-audit HIGH/MEDIUM items verified FIXED in live production
